newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: RALLYING-MAKINEN LEADS AS BIG NAMES RETIRE.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MAKINEN LEADS AS BIG NAMES RETIRE.

text.p: World champion Tommi Makinen took advantage of his rivals' problems to lead the Portuguese Rally after 10 eventful stages on Monday.

The Finn, in a Mitsubishi, overhauled Subaru driver Kenneth Eriksson of Sweden on the ninth stage after a day of hard driving in dry, dusty conditions, and had gained a five seconds lead by the end of the 10th.
After the retirements of championship leader Colin McRae of Britain and second-placed Spaniard Carlos Sainz, a victory for Makinen would be enough for him to take command of the world series.
Makinen was bidding to relaunch his challenge in the fourth event of the season following a disappointing start to the year.

McRae had been leading when his Subaru stopped near the finish of the sixth stage with engine problems. Although he was able to push the car to the end of the stage, he did not reach the service point in time and was forced to drop out.
"It's more than a disappointment," the Scot said. "Everything felt good on this event and we were pulling out a good lead."
Sainz had been in contention early on but encountered gearbox problems with his Ford on the fifth stage.
"Everything was going fine in the stage and it would have been a good time, but just two kilometres from the end there was a big bang in the transmission," said the Spaniard.
"Maybe something in the gearbox tried to seize, but there was nothing we could do and I was forced to park the car."
